# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_021_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 21

**1** Mary said to Jesus: "What are your disciples like?"

**2** He said: "They're like children who've set up camp in a field that isn't theirs.

**3** When the owners arrive and say, 'Give us our field back,' the children strip off their clothes right in front of them and hand the field back.

**4** So I say: if the owner of a house knows a thief is on the way, he'll stay awake and won't let the thief break in and steal his things.

**5** You — stay alert against the world. Equip yourselves with real strength; don't let the robbers find a way to get to you. The trouble you're dreading will come.

**6** Have someone in your group who knows what to do.

**7** When the grain was ready, he came fast, sickle in hand, and cut it down. Anyone with ears, listen."

---

**Translation Notes (PNEUMA):**
- "Set up camp" — more transient and informal than "settled"
- "Strip off their clothes right in front of them" — the nakedness is deliberate, immediate, shameless
- "Break in" — "dig through" rendered as breaking in; common burglary method
- "Real strength" — "great strength" rendered with emphasis on authenticity
- "The trouble you're dreading" — the difficulty is anticipated with apprehension
